title: Washington's farewell address discusses the posture of affairs with foreign nations
summary: Washington's 1796 farewell treats relations with foreign nations as a central warning.
body: Washington's 1796 farewell, as Avalon prints it, speaks of the posture of affairs with foreign nations as a reason for his choices, and warns about permanent foreign attachments in the course of the address. The address is advice, not a statute. The wording on the page includes: "greater security from external danger, a less frequent interruption of their peace by foreign nations; and, what is of inestimable value, they must derive from union an exemption from those broils and wars between themselves, which so frequently afflict neighboring countries not tied together by the same governments, which their own rival ships alone would".
